sources.title: Stephen C. Druce, The Lands West of the Lakes: A History of the Ajattappareng Kingdoms, 1200 to 1600 (2009), chapter 5
sources.note: Direct full publisher chapter, printed pages 201 onward. Early settlement and agricultural organization, trade, rivers, forest clearance and risks. Entire book and thesis predecessor treated as one work for budgets. Interpretive language preserved.

sources.title: Muhammad Nur, Akin Duli and Yusriana, Changes in the Utilization of the Proto-Historical Landscape, Soppeng Regency (2021)
sources.note: Direct publisher article PDF at /article/125967719.pdf, pages 334 to 339. Sewo landscape transition, megaliths, methods and fourteenth-century rice development are researchers’ interpretation, not a precisely dated royal decree.

sources.title: David Bulbeck and Ian Caldwell, Oryza sativa and the origins of kingdoms in South Sulawesi (2008)
sources.note: Original ANU author abstract; DOI 10.1080/13639810802016117. Rice husk phytolith evidence at Allangkanangnge and interpretation of indigenous agrarian development.

sources.title: David Bulbeck and Ian Caldwell, The indigenous fortifications of South Sulawesi, in Forts and Fortification in Wallacea (2020)
sources.note: Direct full ANU publisher chapter. Background history, bilateral descent groups, Table 7.2 Bulu Matanre fourteenth to seventeenth centuries, defended pass, later Goa/Talloq expansion and Islamization. Whole edited volume grouped.

sources.title: Stephen C. Druce, Exploring Early Political and Economic Ties between West Soppéng and Suppaq (2001)
sources.note: Original scholar PDF indexed pages 36 and 38. Direct site challenge. Royal genealogies, Wé Tékéwanua traditions and explicit doubts about first four generations. Note 3 says the Attoriolonna Soppéng was probably first written in the eighteenth century.

sources.title: Ian Caldwell, South Sulawesi A.D. 1300 to 1600: Ten Bugis Texts (1988), corrected transcription, section 2.5
sources.note: Full original indexed section 2.5, also /terjemahan/theses/caldwell-1988.pdf; direct fetch fails. Exact opening Iana sureq poadaqadaqéngngi tanaé ri Soppéng and translation; nineteenth-century manuscript copies and Matthes 1864 pages 520 to 523. No reconstruction of Bugis glyphs or claim of contemporary fourteenth-century surviving copy.

sources.title: Wasita, The Problem of Patih Muhur’s Carbon Dating and Its Position in the Historical Kingdoms of South Kalimantan (2015)
sources.note: Direct PDF article/download/5733/4177, printed pages 20 to 25. Ulin posts, kalang-sunduk braces, galam supports, uncalibrated 640 ± 110 BP translated by article as 1200 to 1420 CE; source calls for reassessment and more samples. Do not present this as calibrated secure site chronology or proven Nagara Daha port. Site just outside atlas polygon, clearly comparison.

sources.title: Ni Komang Ayu Astiti, Pusat kerajaan Kutai Kartanegara abad XIII to XVII, Universitas Indonesia thesis
sources.note: Institutional full abstract indexed/direct PDF /file?file=pdf%2Fabstrak%2Fid_abstrak-20251382.pdf: traditional 1300 start from Salasilah Kutai, later capital moves and reconstruction limits. Abstract has incorrect century labels beside dates; century labels not adopted. Later Islamic town morphology not projected into 1300.

sources.title: Ni Komang Ayu Astiti, Archaeological Resources of Kutai Kartanegara (2018), Naditira Widya 12.1
sources.note: Direct full PDF /article/download/5695/4150. Pages 76 to 77 and 80 on changing river centres and mixed archaeological heritage. This is a different 2018 heritage paper from the earlier UI thesis. Claims placing Islam in thirteenth century not adopted. Object inventories not assigned a common medieval date.

sources.title: Leiden University Libraries, The Asian Library brochure: La Galigo manuscript
sources.note: Original university brochure full indexed text: Bugis-language epic, twelve volumes, transcription by Colliq Pujie, Queen Mother of Tanete, commissioned by B. F. Matthes. Explicit nineteenth-century later witness.

proposedOverrides.summary: Distinct Borneo and Sulawesi societies with growing agricultural kingdoms and maritime connections.

batchIdentityNotes: Exact indexed label 1300 to 1492, alias var kingdoms. No shared-card association. Public geometry distinguishes earlier Sumatra/Malay record and mixed India/islands record. Sites tested: Soppeng, Gowa, Bantaeng, Allangkanangnge, Suppaq, Kutai Lama inside both snapshots. Patih Muhur is outside and a named comparison only. Surviving manuscript witness is later; no 1300s original Bugis manuscript claimed. No hospital, toilet, universal religious identity or household custom invented. Modern object inventories and nineteenth-century learning explicitly dated/scoped.
